newsitem.title: FRANCE: Caisse des Depots (CDC) nearly doubles profits.
newsitem.headline: Caisse des Depots (CDC) nearly doubles profits.

text.p: State-owned Caisse des Depots et Consignations (CDC) nearly doubled its net attributable profit in 1996 and expects to show about the same profit this year, managing director Philippe Lagayette said on Tuesday.
Profits were 3.97 billion francs ($690.7 million) last year, a 90 percent increase, the financial institution reported in a statement.

"The group's earnings capacity is solid for years to come," Lagayette told a news conference. "For this year, barring a major change in the situation in financial markets, the group expects a result of the same order of magnitude as 1996."
Profits were driven primarily by the CDC's core banking and financial activities, which accounted for 3.55 billion francs.
Investments and subsidiaries' activities brought in 417 million francs. The results included provisions for 1.2 billion francs for real estate activities.
State-owned insurer Caisse Nationale de Prevoyance (CNP) kicked in 468 million francs versus 428 million francs during the year-earlier period.
CNP's turnover from personal insurance policies was 100 billion francs for 1996, assuring it remained France's largest in that field, officials said.
Lagayette said CDC hoped to increase its stake in CNP to a little over 35 percent in case the government decides to privatise CNP.
"I would like to see CNP privatised...but to assure the continuation of close ties with CNP, CDC would have to increase its holdings to a little over 35 percent," he said.
CDC now holds 30 percent of CNP.
